# Security policy

The JoomGallery friends maintainers take reports of potential security vulnerabilities seriously. Thank you for helping protect websites that use JoomGallery.

## Privately report a vulnerability

**Do not disclose a suspected vulnerability in a public GitHub issue, pull request, forum post, or social media message before coordinating with the maintainers.**

Use a private channel to contact the current maintainers:

- **Preferred if enabled:** [Report a vulnerability through GitHub's private reporting interface](https://github.com/JoomGalleryfriends/JoomGallery/security/advisories/new).
- **Contact form:** Contact the maintainer team through the official [contact form](https://www.joomgalleryfriends.net/en/contact.html).
- **Alternative:** Contact the maintainer team through the official mail team[AT]joomgalleryfriends.net.

## What to include in a report

Please provide as much of the following as you can, without putting real users or production systems at risk:

- A concise description of the vulnerability and its potential impact.
- Affected JoomGallery version(s), Joomla version, PHP version and relevant configuration.
- Reproduction steps or a minimal proof of concept on a test system.
- Whether authentication, special permissions or unusual configuration are required.
- Relevant screenshots or logs, with credentials and sensitive data removed.
- Your preferred contact method and whether you would like public credit after the fix.

Avoid sending passwords, access tokens, private images, personal data or data taken from third-party systems. Do not attempt to access or modify data that is not yours.

## What happens next

1. We will send you a confirmation of receipt within days of receiving the message.
2. The maintainers review the report, assess the impact, affected versions and potential mitigation.
3. A fix is prepared and reviewed privately where possible, before public disclosure.
4. A security release and advisory are coordinated. We collaborate with the [Joomla! Security Strike Team](https://developer.joomla.org/security) on disclosures and CVEs.
5. Users are informed through official releases, Joomla update mechanisms where applicable, and the project website.

This work is performed by volunteers, so response and remediation times vary. **The team does not promise a fixed response or release deadline.** If you do not receive a response after a reasonable period, follow up through the same private channel rather than publishing details immediately.

## Coordinated disclosure and credit

We ask security researchers to allow maintainers a reasonable opportunity to assess and fix a reported issue before public disclosure. Please coordinate timing and technical details with the team.

If you would like attribution, include your preferred name or handle in your report. The team will happily credit in the advisory or release announcement, but will respect a request to remain anonymous.

## Supported versions

Security fixes normally target currently supported releases. **Consult the [latest releases](https://github.com/JoomGalleryfriends/JoomGallery/releases) and the [project website](https://www.joomgalleryfriends.net/) for up-to-date compatibility and support information.** Unsupported versions may not receive fixes.

## Non-security issues

For ordinary bugs, usability problems and feature suggestions, use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/JoomGalleryfriends/JoomGallery/issues) or the [community support forum](https://www.forum.joomgalleryfriends.net/). Please do not use public issue trackers for exploitable vulnerability details.
